metadata.case_name: HO HO MING v. TSEPOWAH AND OTHERS

injuries.description: 4 cm long laceration wound over the left parietal region of his head
source: There was a 4 cm long laceration wound over the left parietal region of his head, swelling and tenderness over his left shoulder with associated dilated left upper limb veins, tenderness over chest wall and abrasion over his right knee.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

source: CT scan of brain showed tiny left parietal contusion.

injuries.description: fractures of left clavicle and fractures of 2nd to 6th ribs
source: X-rays showed fractures of left clavicle and fractures of 2nd to 6th ribs.

injuries.description: tear of the left axillary artery; vascular injury to left arm requiring grafting
source: An arteriogram showed a tear of the left axillary artery.
Vein graft was done for repairing of the torn axillary vein.

An arteriogram for the left arm was repeated on 27 November 2000 which showed acutely truncated left axillary artery with 3rd part of axillary artery reconstituted by collaterals. The distal arteries were markedly narrowed.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of other specified blood vessels at shoulder or upper arm level

injuries.description: severe injury to the left brachial plexus with rupture of all the three main trunks of the plexus; complete avulsion of neurovascular bundle to the left arm
injuries.body_part: left brachial plexus / left upper limb
source: Emergency surgery, carried out by vascular surgeon on the same day as the plaintiff was admitted, revealed complete avulsion of neurovascular bundle to the left arm.

Surgical exploration of the left shoulder was carried out on 14 December 2000 and it was found that there was a severe injury to the left brachial plexus with rupture of all the three main trunks of the plexus.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of multiple nerves at shoulder or upper arm level

manifestations.description: complete loss of movement and sensation of left arm
arterial pulses of his left arm were absent (both brachial and radial pulse)
severe neuralgic pain of his left hand
wasting of the limb, poor sensation or complete absence of it, poor grip or total inability to grip and severe weakness

treatments_received: Emergency surgery (vascular) on the day of admission
Vein graft for torn axillary vein
Transfer to Prince of Wales Hospital
Nerve grafting to musculocutaneous, radial and medial nerves
Tendon transfer, 1st carpo-metacarpal joint fusion and split distal FPL tenodesis, rerouting of biceps tendon (29 July 2004)
Free microvascular transfer of gracilis muscle (February 2006)
treatments_future: symptomatic treatment of the neurotic pain of the left upper limb
periodic occupational therapy/physiotherapy (10 days' treatment once every six months)
rehabilitation training (three sessions per week for six months)

losses.description: Almost complete loss of use of his left arm
Will not be able to return to his pre-accident job as a scaffold dismantler
Moderately severe adjustment disorder with mixed depressive and anxiety features; low self esteem, bleak future outlook, gloom and sadness
